statement: An HTTP request authenticated into a server-derived security context at the single node data-plane ingress whose method and static path uniquely match an immutable request Binding is resolved by RequestBindingRouteResolver to a current ready Cell, dispatched as a canonical Service_Message through ServiceDispatcher and MessageRouter to the parent-owned runtime invocation owner, and returns the genuine component's status, headers, and body; the live minimal-deployment-request-cell-routing scenario observes that response before and after replica handoff, processed completion rather than transport ACK as success, and zero component invocations for unmatched or ambiguous routes.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Consume the genuine component execution and ready/running Cell contract established by minimal-deployment-request-cell-runtime-readiness; do not recreate component loading, runtime lifecycle, services actual, or readiness decisions in the routing layer.

Use exactly one HTTP normalization adapter followed by RequestBindingRouteResolver, ServiceDispatcher, MessageRouter, and the selected runtime invocation owner; direct MessageRouter calls from HTTP ingress, direct local handler calls, ad-hoc sockets, service-endpoint bypasses, and old-path fallback are forbidden.

Authentication must derive and freeze tenant, principal, and roles on the server, authorize the request action through ServiceDispatcher, and reject client-supplied tenant, principal, Binding identity, target identity, or owner outcomes as authority.
Route resolution must consume the immutable request Binding and owner-produced actuals without adding mutable route ingress, statement-scoped Bindings, shadow route tables, or reader-side repair.

RequestBindingRouteResolver and the receiving runtime invocation owner must validate the same tenant, Binding version, derived service identity, replica actual identity, and active or ready state; the receiver must revalidate locally after awaits and immediately before component execution, and a stale, moved, or superseded actual must return a typed retryable outcome without invoking.

HTTP success requires processed component-response evidence carrying the component-produced status, headers, and body; acknowledged transport alone is never success, and no-handler, handler-error, timeout, late-response, stale-target, and unavailable-target outcomes must retain typed retryable, terminal, or ambiguous classifications.

One invocation identity must bind tenant, Binding version, method, path, and canonical request digest; concurrent or replayed delivery must use a durable single-winner or equally strong duplicate-effect fence, reject the same identity with different intent, suppress redrive after late success, and never retry after ambiguous dispatch unless the receiver can return the original result without repeating effects.

Selection, dispatch, redirect, and response wait must inherit one caller deadline and explicit attempt ceiling without nested fresh budgets; counters reset only on processed completion, every stop is typed and observable, and shutdown cancels and cleans pending requests, retries, dedup claims, and late-response waiters without dropping a completed result.

Reuse MessageRouter pressure and admission semantics, bound per-target and total in-flight request work and retry volume, and emit structured overload before timeout; routing must not add an unbounded queue or infer overload only from deadline expiry.

The proof must go red at the engaged route or delivery assertion, use contract-backed router stubs where a real transport seam is not used, preserve deadline and retry ordering under compressed time, include every Binding and actual admission field, prove handoff retires the old target and invokes the genuine component on the new target, prove returned status, headers, and body are component-produced, keep unmatched and ambiguous invocation counts at zero, and replay no-handler, late response, restart, and concurrent retry orderings.
Activation of change, time, once, boot, call, and pushdown Bindings and elastic learner placement remain outside this Quest.
